key_insight: Two-phase LES reveals that the bubble-curtain “breakthrough” regime actually splits into three distinct subregimes, governed by both air Froude number and salt-to-freshwater density ratio.
engineering_relevance: Bubble-curtain performance in ship locks cannot be optimized using air Froude number alone; the density ratio also strongly affects salt transport blocking efficiency.
method: Two-phase large-eddy simulations of a laboratory lock-exchange setup
Detailed analysis of flow and density fields around a bubble curtain
Regime identification across varying air Froude number and salt-freshwater density ratio
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation-based hydrodynamic and transport results showing three subregimes and differing salt-blocking effectiveness across parameter variations.
watch_item: Results are based on laboratory-scale simulations, so scale-up to full ship-lock operations may require additional validation under real operating conditions.
paper_title: Lock-exchange flow regimes under low air Froude number bubble curtains
